title: Division with Remainders
description: Master division with remainders for Class 4 Maths. Learn to divide 3-digit numbers by 1-digit, interpret remainders in word problems with the D-M-S-B-R method. Includes 10 MCQs and 6 IMO questions.

topics.title: Divide 3-Digit by 1-Digit (Long Division)
topics.concept:
Division means splitting a number into equal groups. When we divide a 3-digit number by a 1-digit number, we use long division with the D-M-S-B-R method:

  • D = Divide
  • M = Multiply
  • S = Subtract
  • B = Bring down
  • R = Repeat (or Remainder)

The dividend is the number being divided. The divisor is what we divide by. The quotient is the answer. The remainder is what is left over.

Check: (Divisor x Quotient) + Remainder = Dividend

examples.solution: Divide 8 by 7: quotient 1, remainder 1. Bring down 4 -> 14. Divide 14 by 7: quotient 2, remainder 0. Bring down 7 -> 7. Divide 7 by 7: quotient 1, remainder 0. Answer: 847 / 7 = 121. Check: 7 x 121 = 847.
Divide 4 by 6: cannot, so use 45. 45/6=7, remainder 3. Bring down 3 -> 33. 33/6=5, remainder 3. Answer: Quotient 75, Remainder 3. So 453 = (6 x 75) + 3. Check: 450 + 3 = 453.

examples.problem: A school has 756 books to be arranged equally on 9 shelves. How many books per shelf?
examples.solution: Divide 756 by 9. 7/9: cannot, use 75. 75/9=8 R3. Bring down 6 -> 36. 36/9=4 R0. Answer: 84 books per shelf. Check: 9 x 84 = 756.

recap: D-M-S-B-R: Divide, Multiply, Subtract, Bring down, Repeat
The remainder must always be less than the divisor
Check: Divisor x Quotient + Remainder = Dividend
If a digit is smaller than the divisor, bring down the next digit

topics.title: Interpreting Remainders in Word Problems
topics.concept:
When solving word problems with division, the remainder can mean different things depending on the context. There are three rules:

  • Rule 1 — Ignore: When the question asks for 'full groups' or 'complete sets'. The remainder is not counted. E.g. how many full boxes?
  • Rule 2 — Round Up: When the question asks 'how many needed for everyone'. Even one extra person needs one more group. E.g. how many buses/taxis?
  • Rule 3 — Keep: When the question asks 'how much is left over' or 'how much does each get'. E.g. how many rupees each? How much left?

examples.problem: A farmer has 175 apples. He packs them in bags of 8 each. How many full bags can he make? How many apples are left?
examples.solution: 175 / 8 = 21 remainder 7. Full bags = 21 (Rule 1 - ignore the 7 leftover apples for the bag count). Apples left over = 7 (Rule 3 - keep the remainder). Answer: 21 full bags with 7 apples left.

examples.problem: 175 people need to cross a river. Each boat carries 8 people. How many boat trips are needed?
examples.solution: 175 / 8 = 21 remainder 7. Since all 175 people must cross, the 7 extra people need one more trip. Apply Rule 2 (round up): 21 + 1 = 22. Answer: 22 boat trips.

examples.problem: Rs.1,000 is shared equally among 6 friends. How much does each get? How much is left?
examples.solution: 1000 / 6 = 166 remainder 4. Each friend gets Rs.166 (quotient). Rs.4 is left over (Rule 3 - keep remainder). Answer: Rs.166 each, Rs.4 remaining.

recap: Rule 1 (Ignore): Use when question asks for 'full' or 'complete' groups
Rule 2 (Round up): Use when everyone must be included (buses, taxis, rows)
Rule 3 (Keep): Use when question asks what is left over
The same division can have different answers depending on context!

topics.title: Divisibility and Finding Quotient Patterns
topics.concept:
A number is exactly divisible by another when the remainder is 0. Knowing divisibility rules helps you divide quickly.

Quick Divisibility Rules:

  • Divisible by 2: last digit is 0,2,4,6,8
  • Divisible by 5: last digit is 0 or 5
  • Divisible by 9: sum of digits is divisible by 9
  • Divisible by 10: last digit is 0

The relationship between division and multiplication: if A / B = C, then B x C = A.

examples.problem: Is 648 divisible by 9? Verify by division.
examples.solution: Sum of digits: 6+4+8=18. 18 is divisible by 9. So 648 is divisible by 9. Verify: 648 / 9 = 72 with remainder 0. Check: 9 x 72 = 648.

examples.problem: A number when divided by 7 gives quotient 58 and remainder 4. Find the number.
examples.solution: Using the formula: Number = (Divisor x Quotient) + Remainder = (7 x 58) + 4 = 406 + 4 = 410.

examples.problem: Find the smallest 3-digit number exactly divisible by 8.
examples.solution: 100 / 8 = 12 R4. So 100 is not divisible by 8. To find the next: 8 x 13 = 104. Check: 104 / 8 = 13 R0. Answer: 104.

recap: A number with remainder 0 is exactly divisible by the divisor
Divisibility by 2: even last digit; by 5: last digit 0 or 5; by 9: digit sum divisible by 9
Division and multiplication are inverse operations

questions.explanation: 1000 / 6 = 166 R4. Each gets Rs.166 and Rs.4 is left (Rule 3 — keep remainder).

questions.explanation: Let quotient = remainder = x (where x < 9). Number = 9x + x = 10x. For x=8: number=80. 80/9=8 R8. Largest valid answer is 80.

questions.q: What is the remainder when the product of 15 and 23 is divided by 8?
Divisor = 6, quotient = 84, remainder = 5. If we add 10 to the dividend and divide by 6 again, the new remainder is:
questions.explanation: Original dividend = (6 x 84) + 5 = 509. New dividend = 519. 519 / 6 = 86 R3.

questions.q: Which is ALWAYS true about remainders?
options: Remainder is always less than the divisor
Remainder is always less than quotient
questions.explanation: By definition, remainder must be less than divisor. If remainder >= divisor, we can divide further.

questions.q: A number leaves remainder 3 when divided by 5 AND remainder 2 when divided by 4. The smallest such number is:
questions.explanation: Check 18: 18/5=3R3 and 18/4=4R2. Both conditions satisfied. 13: 13/4=3R1 (fails). 18 is the smallest.
